:::{#thm-kernel-same-mode}
#### A density and its kernel have the same modes

If $g$ is a [kernel of the density](#def-kernel) $f$ of a [random variable](#def-random-variable) $X$,
then the [modes](#def-mode) of $f$ are the elements of the [argmax](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra.html#def-argmax) of $g$ over the [range](#def-range) of $X$:

$$\modef{f} = \argmax_{x \in \rangef{X}} g(x).$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Write $f(x) = c\, g(x)$ with $c > 0$ (@def-kernel).
For any $x$, multiplying both sides of $g(x^*) \ge g(x)$ by $c > 0$
gives $f(x^*) \ge f(x)$,
and dividing by $c$ reverses this.
So $f(x^*) \ge f(x)$ for every $x$ exactly when $g(x^*) \ge g(x)$ for every $x$.
By the definition of the [argmax](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra.html#def-argmax),
these are the conditions $x^* \in \argmax_{x \in \rangef{X}} f(x)$ and $x^* \in \argmax_{x \in \rangef{X}} g(x)$.

:::
